title: How to export the game created in rpg maker xp

posts.author: ini
posts.body: Hi guys, I have a question that even though I have researched on the net and sometimes found ways to get around it, it doesn't always work. How do I export the game that I create so that someone who doesn't have the tool can play without errors or problems?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Isn't it right in the instruction manual?
In the newer makers it's called deployment, but in VX Ace it's called Compress Game Data - it should be right in your file menu.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Turan is correct, the command in XP is "compress game data." You have the option to encrypt the game, but otherwise there's not much to it.
Turan is also correct that we'll need more information on what the problem us before we can help you troubleshoot it!
EDIT: it sounds like you might be running into a problem with the RTP! XP and VX/A use an actual  "run-time package," the default assets saved out separately to reduce download sizes. If you don't remove the games dependence on the RTP, players will need to have it installed in order for the game to run.
I'm not at a computer now to get the screenshot of the exact menu, but somewhere (Game, maybe?) there's an option to select up to 3 RTPs. If you've used any of the default resources in your project, you'll need to manually import them, then set the RTP used by the project to "None."
If that sounds like your issue, I can give more detailed instructions later! If not, we'll definitely need more details.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
to give some background for the RTP issue:
RMXP was at a time when most people were at dial-up and flatrates were unknown. So the size of the downloads was much more important than today.
as a partial solution the option of "create game archive" could be used with or without RTP included.
inclusion of the RTP increased its size a lot, but made the game independently working - this was for people who only rarely downloaded RPG-Maker-games.
not including the RTP required the RTP to be downloaded independently - that independent download is still available in the downloads on top of this site. The advantage of that was that you only needed one RTP installed for all games done with RMXP, reducing your total download when playing multiple RMXP games.
with toiday's download rates it is usually better to include the RTP in the archive because no one bothers anymore about a few hundred MB of extra download.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
A missing file is exactly what it sounds like: the game can't find something that it needs. Knowing the name of the file would be a big help, but it still sounds like it's probably an issue with the game requiring the RTP, and the player not having it installed.
The RTP includes all of the resources that come with RMXP by default. Anything that was there when you first created the project is part of the RTP. You can identify RTP resources in the Material Base by the color of the dot next to the file name--RTP-dependent files have a blue dot next to them, whereas files that you imported yourself have a red dot.
Here you can see that I have all of the default resources, plus a custom one called "AlchemyWorkshop."
When you go to Game > Select RTP, you get this menu:
And as you mentioned, if you set RTP 1 to (None), all of the default resources--the ones with blue dots--disappear. As long as there's an RTP set in this menu, the game will require that RTP.
If your game
does
require the RTP, the
player
will need to
download and install it from here
. (Scroll down, select Run-Time Package, and then select RMXP.) Installing the RTP ensures that all those assets end up in the place on the player's computer where the game will know to look for them.
If you want your game to run
without
the RTP--which you do!--you'll need to tell the game to not require one. The easiest way I've found is to export all of the default resources from the Material Base, then re-import those files. You'll see that the dots next to them in the Material Base turn red. That means that they are will no longer disappear when you set RTP 1 to (None), therefore nothing you've built will change.
You can theoretically import only the default files that you know you've used, but it only adds about 30mb to your total file size to include all of the default resources. As Andar said: when RMXP was new in 2006, 30mb was quite a lot to download. And it would add up quickly if you had those same files in every game you downloaded. But these days, 30mb is nothing to worry about.
I hope that solves your problem!

posts.author: ini

TeiRaven said:
Um arquivo faltando é exatamente o que parece: o jogo não consegue encontrar algo que precisa. Saber o nome do arquivo seria uma grande ajuda, mas ainda parece que provavelmente é um problema com o jogo exigindo o RTP, e o jogador não o tendo instalado.
O RTP inclui todos os recursos que vêm com o RMXP por padrão. Tudo o que estava lá quando você criou o projeto pela primeira vez faz parte do RTP. Você pode identificar os recursos do RTP na Material Base pela cor do ponto ao lado do nome do arquivo — arquivos dependentes do RTP têm um ponto azul ao lado deles, enquanto arquivos que você importou têm um ponto vermelho.
View attachment 323964
Aqui você pode ver que tenho todos os recursos padrão, além de um personalizado chamado "AlchemyWorkshop".
Quando você vai em Jogo > Selecionar RTP, você vê este menu:
View attachment 323965
E como você mencionou, se você definir RTP 1 para (Nenhum), todos os recursos padrão--aqueles com pontos azuis--desaparecem. Enquanto houver um RTP definido neste menu, o jogo exigirá esse RTP.
Se o seu jogo
exigir
o RTP, o
jogador
precisará
baixá-lo e instalá-lo aqui
. (Role para baixo, selecione Pacote de tempo de execução e, em seguida, selecione RMXP.) A instalação do RTP garante que todos esses ativos acabem no local no computador do jogador onde o jogo saberá procurá-los.
Se você quiser que seu jogo rode
sem
o RTP--o que você quer!--você precisará dizer ao jogo para não exigir um. A maneira mais fácil que eu encontrei é exportar todos os recursos padrão da Material Base e então reimportar esses arquivos. Você verá que os pontos próximos a eles na Material Base ficam vermelhos. Isso significa que eles não desaparecerão mais quando você definir o RTP 1 como (Nenhum), portanto nada que você construiu mudará.
Você pode teoricamente importar apenas os arquivos padrão que você sabe que usou, mas isso só adiciona cerca de 30mb ao tamanho total do seu arquivo para incluir todos os recursos padrão. Como Andar disse: quando o RMXP era novo em 2006, 30mb era bastante para baixar. E aumentaria rapidamente se você tivesse esses mesmos arquivos em todos os jogos que você baixou. Mas hoje em dia, 30mb não é nada para se preocupar.
Espero que isso resolva seu problema!
